description: RWS · Situation/Advice/Outcome · a job decision with a note that leads.

detail: If the fear is the move rather than the work, what specifically about moving are you picturing — and how much of it is about the first month rather than the years after?
If you stayed, what would be slowly crumbling in the background that The Tower reversed might be pointing at?
In the Six of Wands scene, who do you imagine standing along the route — and whose acknowledgement would actually change how the decision feels?

output.synthesis: Steady skill built by repetition sits behind you; The Tower reversed suggests a change being postponed rather than escaped, and the Six of Wands points to recognition if the momentum continues.

per_card.text: In the Past position, the Eight of Pentacles suggests that what shaped this question is diligence — the craft you've built by doing the thing again and again, quietly and well. That patient apprenticeship may be why a job in Lisbon is even on the table; the skill is already yours and travels with you. It also hints that mastery, for you, has come from the next repetition rather than a leap, which may be part of why a leap now feels foreign.
nuances: One way to read it: the focus that served you may also have become a comfortable groove, and the question is whether Lisbon extends the craft or interrupts it.
Alternatively, the card may point less to your job history than to a longer habit of earning things slowly, which could make a sudden offer feel unearned.

per_card.text: You said it yourself: "The Tower again, but reversed this time. I think the fear is the move, not the work" — and the reference reading supports you, since reversed this card may point to an upheaval being postponed rather than avoided. What is most active right now seems to be the resistance itself: the slow crumble of a situation you're bracing against rather than the work you'd actually be doing. It may also be read the other way, that the worst of the shake-up has already passed and what remains is the fear's echo.
nuances: One plausible alternative: the postponed collapse isn't the move but staying — the current arrangement quietly giving way while you decide.
The Mars and fire correspondence suggests heat and urgency in this moment; you might notice whether that pressure is coming from the offer's deadline or from inside you.

per_card.text: In the Future position, the Six of Wands suggests one direction this could take if the present momentum continues: progress that others can see, and the confidence that follows being met with approval. Given the Eight of Pentacles behind you, this may read as the private craft finally becoming public — work acknowledged rather than just done. The card's own caution is worth keeping: notice who would be celebrating with you and who would only be watching from a distance.
nuances: One way to read it: the recognition may arrive whether or not you move, if it's the work rather than the location that's landing.
Alternatively, the visibility itself could be the challenge — a more public, acknowledged role may ask a different kind of confidence than the quiet focus you've practised.

output.combined: Read along the line, these three suggest a situation that has been moving from private mastery toward visible recognition, with the present caught in a held breath. The Eight of Pentacles gives you a past of earned, repeated skill; The Tower reversed suggests that the change is being postponed rather than escaped, which sits closely with your own note that the fear is the move and not the work; the Six of Wands offers one possible direction where the work you've done is acknowledged openly. What the line does not settle is whether Lisbon is the location of that recognition or simply the loudest option on the table right now. You might ask yourself whether the thing you're bracing against is the flight and the unfamiliar street, or something in the current arrangement that is already quietly giving way.
